description:
The /fly HUD speed readout displays 'NaN km/s' throughout the entire flight for missions to outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres, and any destination whose orbital radius exceeds ~1.5 AU). Inner-planet destinations (Mercury, Venus) produce finite but physically incorrect values because the same Mars-hardcoded semi-major axis is used.

Expected: The HUD speed readout shows a finite, physically plausible speed (km/s) consistent with a Hohmann transfer from Earth to the specific destination, for every mission in the catalog. Earth→Mars missions are unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
- For every mission file under static/data/missions/ {jupiter, saturn, uranus, neptune, pluto, ceres, asteroid} (and any future outer-planet destination), heliocentricKms is a finite number (not NaN, not Infinity) at every simDay along the trajectory. [reporter: Issue states: 'the HUD speed readout just says NaN km/s the whole way' — NaN is the reported symptom.]
- For every Earth→Mars mission (static/data/missions/mars/), heliocentricKms is identical to the pre-fix value within numerical precision (no regression). [code-invariant: Mars missions currently work; a fix must not regress existing correct behavior.]
- For Mercury and Venus missions, heliocentricKms is finite and consistent with the Hohmann transfer semi-major axis (R_EARTH_AU + R_DEST_AU) / 2 from the DESTINATIONS table in src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts. [repo-data: static/data/planets.json defines Mercury a=0.3871, Venus a=0.7233; DESTINATIONS re-exports these as DestinationConstants.a (src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts lines 69-77). The vis-viva formula in src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts defines heliocentricSpeed(r, a).]
